title: Inference routing safety and observability invariants - design notes
agenda: Quick context recap: recent incidents where routing fallback caused metric drift
Proposed invariants for safe routing decisions and observable checks
Telemetry signals we must capture at each routing handoff
Decision matrix for automatic fallback vs manual intervention
Action item assignments and short-term experiments
summary: Meeting to converge on a minimal set of safety invariants and telemetry guarantees for inference request routing. Goal: reduce silent regressions when automated fallbacks or regional routing triggers occur, and to make decision boundaries auditable and observable for operators and product owners.
discussion_points: Incident recap: fallback to smaller model variant in us-east caused subtle hallucination increases for a subset of enterprise customers; SLI drift not surfaced until daily aggregation

Root cause hypothesis: routing trigger threshold relied solely on per-shard compute utilization and didn't consider quality regression signals (eval hooks missing), and trace sampling rate was too low for short-lived fallbacks

Proposal: define routing safety invariants that must hold before executing an automated fallback: 1) per-route quality delta below configured threshold, 2) latency SLO breach sustained > 30s, 3) KV-cache warmness below threshold (for variants that require expensive rewarm), 4) end-to-end trace present
Telemetry needed: per-request routing_decision tag, pre/post model variant id, cache_hit_ratio, downstream eval_score hooks (fast approximate scorer), trace_id propagation at each hop

SRE concerns: sampling budget - full trace collection at 100% is too expensive. Proposed adaptive sampling: full traces for routes that changed variant within last 24h or for routes with recent SLO violations; event counters for all requests
Product ask: provide clear rollback semantics for canary fallbacks, and a human-readable reason attached to each automated fallback event for audit and CS handoff
Security/PII: ensure any attached reason or trace does not contain user prompt content; use prompt-hash and metadata only
Edge case: cascading fallbacks across regions leading to oscillation. Suggest global cooldown and jittered backoff per-customer to avoid synchronized flips

Observability invariant: every routing decision must emit a deterministic minimal set of fields in logs/metrics so downstream analytics can reconstruct sequence (timestamp, request_id, route_from, route_to, trigger, pre_metrics, post_metrics)
We should add a small on-path scorer (lightweight quality probe) that runs asynchronously on a sample before fallback is allowed to be used broadly
Operationalizing: expose an admin endpoint to force revert a fallback per-customer and to run a targeted replay of recent requests for debugging
decisions: Adopt the proposed routing safety invariants (quality delta, sustained latency breach, cache warmness, trace presence) as the default gating checks for automated fallback (decision 2025-11-03-01)
Implement adaptive telemetry sampling: full traces for changed routes and SLO-violating routes; 0.5% baseline full-trace sampling for other traffic (decision 2025-11-03-02)
Attach structured 'fallback_reason' metadata (reason_code, prompt_hash, timestamp, decision_version) to every automated fallback event; redact raw prompt text (decision 2025-11-03-03)
Add global cooldown per-customer (default 10 minutes) with exponential backoff jitter to avoid oscillation; expose config in console (decision 2025-11-03-04)
Ship a lightweight async quality probe (alpha) that can approximate eval_score within 50ms on a sampled subset of traffic and gate broad fallback rollout (decision 2025-11-03-05)
Require that any routing change rollout includes a one-week canary with increased telemetry retention and a monitored alerting threshold for quality delta (decision 2025-11-03-06)
risks: Increased sampling and the async probe add compute cost; need to quantify unit-cost impact before wide rollout
False positives from the lightweight probe could unnecessarily block beneficial fallbacks; will need iterative tuning
Exposing fallback_reason metadata increases privacy review surface—engineering must coordinate with security/compliance
Cooldown can delay recovery when real capacity emergencies occur; need override path for SRE on-call
action_items: Aisha: Draft spec for routing safety invariants and publish to Confluence by 2025-11-07
Liam: Prototype the 'fallback_reason' event schema and a minimal SDK change to emit it; checkpoint in PR by 2025-11-10
Emily: Design adaptive sampling algorithm and estimate cost impact; provide numbers by 2025-11-12
Ravi: Define SRE override protocol and implement an admin 'force-revert' endpoint prototype; demo in next on-call rotation (2025-11-09)
Sofia: Add UI/console exposure for cooldown/jitter config and draft small admin workflow for canary revert; proposal by 2025-11-14
All: Run a 48h internal simulation using archived traces to measure oscillation risk and sampling load; start simulation 2025-11-11
notes: We intentionally constrained the safety invariants to be minimal and measurable. The meeting emphasized observability-first: decisions should be reversible and auditable. Avoid vendor-lock assumptions in the probe (keep it model-agnostic). For the alpha probe we'll target a 0.1% traffic sample and evaluate false positive rate over the simulation window. Follow-ups: (1) instrument a dashboard that shows routing decision timelines for a specific request_id, (2) small PR to standardize the 'routing_decision' log key across runtime components.
